classification.difficultyReason: Subtract equations with matching coefficients, then substitute back, including a final exact fractional solution.

content.prompt: Solve the simultaneous equations using the elimination method.

answer.worked:
Subtract the first equation from the second.
$$\begin{align*}(2x+y)-(x+y)&=5-2\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first equation.
$$\begin{align*}3+y&=2\\y&=-1\end{align*}$$
Check: $3+(-1)=2$ and $2(3)+(-1)=5$.

Subtract the second equation from the first.
$$\begin{align*}(3x+2y)-(x+2y)&=13-9\\2x&=4\\x&=2\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the second equation.
$$\begin{align*}2+2y&=9\\2y&=7\\y&=\frac{7}{2}\end{align*}$$
Check: $3(2)+2(\frac{7}{2})=13$ and $2+2(\frac{7}{2})=9$.

Subtract the first equation from the second.
$$\begin{align*}(3x-y)-(2x-y)&=11-9\\x&=2\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first equation.
$$\begin{align*}4-y&=9\\-y&=5\\y&=-5\end{align*}$$
Check: $2(2)-(-5)=9$ and $3(2)-(-5)=11$.

answer.short:
$x=\frac{7}{3},\ y=\frac{11}{12}$.

Subtract the equations to eliminate $y$, then substitute to find $y$.
answer.worked:
Subtract the first equation from the second.
$$\begin{align*}(5x-4y)-(2x-4y)&=8-1\\3x&=7\\x&=\frac{7}{3}\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the first equation.
$$\begin{align*}2\left(\frac{7}{3}\right)-4y&=1\\\frac{14}{3}-4y&=1\\-4y&=-\frac{11}{3}\\y&=\frac{11}{12}\end{align*}$$
Check:
$$\begin{align*}2\left(\frac{7}{3}\right)-4\left(\frac{11}{12}\right)&=1\\5\left(\frac{7}{3}\right)-4\left(\frac{11}{12}\right)&=8\end{align*}$$
